$comment: EXAMPLE — the TextMate injection grammar a third-party package would ship to highlight its `@sql { … }` expression-tier bodies as SQL (expr-tiers / text-tiers arcs). This is the extension mechanism for editor highlighting: a package that declares `@tier(sql, text: "sql", expr: Query)` ships a grammar of this shape, contributed via the VS Code `grammars` contribution point with `injectTo: ["source.noeta"]`. It attaches by textual match (`injectionSelector`), so it needs no change to Noeta's own static grammar — that is why an extension can provide it and the core grammar stays fixed. The body language (`sql` here → `source.sql`) is the tier's declared `text:` language; swap it for `markdown`/`source.yaml`/etc. per tier. Brace counting mirrors the compiler lexer's matching_brace: nested pairs recurse and \{ \} \\ are literal, so a `{…}` in the SQL never ends the block. `${…}` holes are scoped back to `source.noeta`, so a hole highlights as ordinary Noeta inside the SQL — the same split the compiler makes (statics = SQL text, holes = checked Noeta expressions).

tier-escape.$comment: The text-body escapes \{ \} \\ plus \$ (a literal $ that would otherwise open a hole) — matched first so an escaped closer or dollar never triggers a rule below.
tier-escape.name: constant.character.escape.noeta

tier-hole.$comment: A `${ … }` hole is an ordinary Noeta expression — scope its contents back to source.noeta so it highlights as code, not SQL. Nested braces inside the hole are handled by re-including this grammar's brace pair via source.noeta.

tier-brace-pair.$comment: A nested balanced brace pair inside the SQL body — recursion is how TextMate counts depth, so a `{…}` in the text does not close the block.
